question.text: Which of the following is TRUE about SIP (Systematic Investment Plan) in mutual funds?

answer.text: SIP is a separate mutual fund product with its own portfolio
SIP guarantees minimum returns due to rupee cost averaging
SIP can only be done in equity mutual funds
SIP is a method of investing a fixed amount at regular intervals through auto-debit from the investor's bank account

explanation.text: The Logic: SIP is a periodic investment facility — systematic investing through pre-determined contributions at regular intervals. Mutual funds permit SIPs through Post-Dated Cheques (PDCs), NACH mandates, or standing instructions to the bank, and SIP helps with rupee-cost averaging without requiring the investor to time the market. The Trap: SIP is NOT a guaranteed-return product. Marketing materials sometimes overstate the benefits of rupee-cost averaging and lead investors to think SIP eliminates risk; the underlying scheme can still generate negative returns. SIP is also not restricted to equity funds. Note: Encourage consistency over market timing — rupee-cost averaging works best when contributions continue through market downturns.
